statement: arc-24's original enforcer-ui/Cargo.toml declared a hard `enforcer-mcp` path dependency (aspirational, unused by any module — only mentioned in doc prose). g01 needed the OPPOSITE direction (enforcer-mcp -> enforcer-ui, to back the ocentra_enforcer_ui tool with enforcer_ui::serve::ui_tool_response), which is a genuine Cargo cyclic-dependency error with the pre-existing edge still in place. Fix: removed the unused enforcer-mcp dep from enforcer-ui/Cargo.toml (and corrected the stale lib.rs/Cargo.toml prose that referenced it) since arc-24 never actually called into it.
why: Any later g0x/arc pack that declares a dependency direction contrary to what a Track G/F/H MCP tool wiring pass needs will hit the same cyclic-dependency wall; the fix pattern (grep for actual `enforcer_mcp::` usage before assuming a Cargo.toml dep line is load-bearing) generalizes.
howToApply: Before adding a new crate-to-crate Cargo dependency to satisfy a wiring pass, `cargo tree -p <target> -i <dep>` and grep the target crate's src/ for real usage of the dep's namespace; if a conflicting-direction dependency exists but is unused in code, it is safe to remove even though this workpack does not 'own' that manifest line, because the alternative is a hard build failure with no ownership question left to resolve.

evidence.ref: cargo test -p enforcer-mcp: `error: cyclic package dependency: package enforcer-mcp depends on itself` before removing enforcer-ui's unused enforcer-mcp dep line

statement: enforcer-cli's `enforcer serve` bare subcommand was ALREADY locked (by a passing integration test, serve_mode_responds_to_initialize_over_stdio) to mean "start the MCP stdio server" before g01 landed, even though the g01 workpack text says 'enforcer serve and enforcer ui both resolve to this [UI] surface.' Reconciled by adding `--ui` as an opt-in flag on `Command::Serve(ServeArgs)` (bare `serve` still defaults to MCP stdio, unchanged) plus a new `Command::Ui(ServeArgs)` top-level alias that always reaches the UI surface — both `enforcer serve --ui` and `enforcer ui` route through `enforcer_ui::serve::run`/`resolve_bind` identically. This preserves the pre-existing locked test while satisfying the two-spellings requirement.
why: A future Track G/plan-doc author reading 'enforcer serve resolves to the UI surface' literally would break the arc-22 MCP stdio contract test if they made bare `serve` mean UI; this decision + its rationale should stop that from happening again.
howToApply: When a workpack's prose conflicts with an existing PASSING integration test elsewhere in the workspace, grep for the locked behavior first (tests/cli_integration.rs is the arc-22 contract surface) and add an opt-in flag/alias rather than repointing the existing bare subcommand.

evidence.ref: crates/enforcer-cli/tests/cli_integration.rs::serve_mode_responds_to_initialize_over_stdio kept green after the change; new tests ui_remote_host_without_token_refuses_to_start / serve_ui_flag_and_ui_alias_both_reject_remote_without_token_identically added

statement: enforcer-cli already leaked enforcer-coordination into `--features lite` builds before g01 (via enforcer-mcp and enforcer-plan's hard, non-optional path deps on enforcer-coordination), despite the crate's own doc comment claiming lite 'excludes that dependency from the graph entirely.' g01's new enforcer-mcp -> enforcer-ui edge has the identical leak (cargo tree -p enforcer-cli --no-default-features --features lite -i enforcer-ui shows it present). This is a pre-existing architectural gap in the lite/full split, not a regression g01 introduced — fixing it properly requires feature-gating enforcer-mcp's own downstream deps (coordination + ui), which is outside g01's owns: (crates/enforcer-ui/src/serve.rs + the CLI/MCP wiring), not enforcer-mcp's internal feature architecture.
why: Whoever eventually tightens the lite/full split (x04 main-branch-protection CI, or a dedicated lite-binary-size pack) needs to know the split was already broken for coordination before UI was added, so they fix enforcer-mcp's feature gating once for both leaks rather than treating enforcer-ui as the sole culprit.
howToApply: To actually fix: add `full`-style Cargo features to enforcer-mcp gating its enforcer-coordination and enforcer-ui deps + the tools that use them (mirroring enforcer-cli's own full/lite split), then have enforcer-cli's full feature enable enforcer-mcp/full instead of enabling enforcer-coordination/enforcer-ui directly.

evidence.ref: cargo tree -p enforcer-cli --no-default-features --features lite -i enforcer-coordination (and -i enforcer-ui) both show the dependency present despite the lite feature
